title: Words that shift your point of view
meaning: Full conversation and thoughtful attention can help you see what was said differently, even when a new perspective requires an inward pause.
text: Sometimes a detailed reply changes the question that began your conversation. The Empress in the physical position of Vishuddha allows words to unfold: giving examples, clarifying impressions and developing each other’s thoughts. The Hermit in energy supports a wish to understand what matters and what stands behind a sentence. The Hanged Man in emotions describes the suspension of an earlier view. A familiar explanation no longer fits what you have heard. This pause can be a meaningful part of communication even before you have an answer to the new thought.

Imagine discussing silence over dinner together. At first it seems to show a lack of interest, but a fuller account of a crowded day opens another explanation. **Conversation can change the meaning of a silence already shared.** You can pause to let that understanding settle. The evening can continue quietly: what matters is that the silence feels less like a puzzle each person must solve alone.

The difficulty is continuing to seek a deeper version after a simple explanation has already been offered. Thoughtfulness supports the exchange, but further questions can keep both of you suspended. Wanting to understand everything, you may lose sight of an ordinary request for a quiet evening. A clear sentence about a present wish allows the new perspective to meet everyday life.
